title: Linux commit e314dbdc — [NET]: Virtual ethernet device driver

date.notes: Committer date of this preserved object: 2007-10-10T23:47:46Z (David S. Miller); author date: 2007-09-25T23:14:46Z (Pavel Emelyanov). Neither is a first-public-submission, earliest-prototype, deployment or Linus first-parent integration date.

claims_extracted.claim: The commit introduces CONFIG_VETH, veth.o and drivers/net/veth.c as a virtual Ethernet pair driver.
claims_extracted.locator: commit diff: drivers/net/Kconfig, drivers/net/Makefile, new drivers/net/veth.c

claims_extracted.claim: The commit states that a main use is communication between network namespaces and arranges the newlink path to ease peer creation in a separate namespace when namespace support is present.
claims_extracted.notes: Supports intended composition/use, not a descent or causal lineage claim.

claims_extracted.claim: The final driver validates generic IFLA_ADDRESS, uses a VETH_INFO_PEER payload prefixed by ifinfomsg and followed by generic IFLA attributes, and calls rtnl_create_link to create the peer.
claims_extracted.locator: drivers/net/veth.c at this commit: lines 293–302, 315–348 and 352–369; include/net/veth.h lines 4–9
claims_extracted.notes: VETH_INFO_PEER has enum value 1, unlike value 2 and NLA_STRING in the June/July v2.1 patches. The ifinfomsg prefix is at the head of VETH_INFO_PEER, not all IFLA_INFO_DATA; its contents are skipped. This commit does not introduce the helper definition.

claims_extracted.claim: The final file retains the specific credit to Eric W. Biederman for the ethtool interface and exposes peer_ifindex.
claims_extracted.locator: drivers/net/veth.c at this commit: header line 7, peer_ifindex key at line 48 and readout at line 93
claims_extracted.notes: Supports narrow property attribution, not whole-driver etun/OpenVZ descent or byte-identical ethtool code.

notes: Do not convert the namespace wording into a derived-from or caused-by edge. The source proves mainline introduction and contemporary intended use, not first deployment or first prototype. The complete four-file introduction diff was checked. RTM_NRELINK in the commit prose is a contemporary typo, not a separate API. The earlier public messages are separately recorded in SRC-0280 through SRC-0285; no equivalence to Miller's August subsystem object is claimed.
